extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing RCE/CPA practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for treating Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) and Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114, including eligibility, what counts as a proper submission, examiner actions, and correspondence form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA conversion to RCE only for extenuating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not convert an improper CPA into an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) simply because it is requested by the applicant; conversion to an RCE under 37 CFR 1.53(b) will be done only if the applicant shows extenuating circumstances warranting conversion (e.g., restoring the application to pending status and correcting the improper RCE is not possible because the application has issued as a patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.15 to inform applicant that a CPA is being treated as an RCE. Conversion is discretionary and reserved for burdensome situations where restoring the original status is impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE proper requires fee and submission meeting 37 CFR 1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 must include the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission that meets the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111 in order to be proper; if timely filed the finality of the prior Office action will be withdrawn and the submission entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE includes the fee and a timely submission responsive within 1.111, use form paragraph 7.42.04 (after final rejection) or appropriate form paragraphs for other contexts. Mere payment of the fee without a submission that meets 1.111 does not toll prior reply deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE does not toll previous reply deadlines unless submission meets 1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere request for, and payment of, the fee for continued examination will not operate to toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment; the submission meeting the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111 must be timely received to continue prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must verify that the submission is responsive within the meaning of 1.111; otherwise abandonment procedures or improper-RCE treatment apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entries must comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission that is an amendment must comply with the manner of making amendments as set forth in 37 CFR 1.121. The amendment must include markings showing the changes relative to the last entered amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file a single amendment at the time of filing the RCE incorporating all desired changes (including any previously filed unentered after-final amendments) and to instruct not to enter unentered after-final amendments. See MPEP § 714.03 for amendment practice under 1.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt requirement for tolling
rubrics_metrics.description: If reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, then it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is not a bona fide attempt, the RCE should be treated as an improper RCE and a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE), Form PTO-2051, should be prepared and mailed. Example anti-patterns: an IDS only; an amendment that cancels all claims and presents no new or substitute claims. The RCE will not toll the period and the application will be abandoned after the statutory reply period if no compliant submission is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of non-bona fide submissions (improper RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that are not bona fide include an IDS only or an amendment that cancels all claims without presenting new/substitute claims; such submissions will not be considered a bona fide attempt under 37 CFR 1.114(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and mail Form PTO-2051 when RCE is improper. Cite Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co., 265 F.3d 1249, 60 USPQ2d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001) for the Office's refusal to enter certain amendments that are not bona fide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fully responsive but bona fide submissions — shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission is not fully responsive but appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, the applicant should be informed why the submission is not fully responsive and be given a new shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) to complete the reply (per 37 CFR 1.135(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.08 to acknowledge the RCE and set the shortened period. Note that this shortened period may be extended pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-compliant amendments that are bona fide
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed with a submission that is an amendment not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121, but which is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, should be treated as a proper RCE and a Notice of Noncompliant Amendment should be mailed to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is given one month or thirty days from the mailing date of the notice (whichever is longer) to provide an amendment complying with 1.121. See MPEP § 714.03 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claims for a different invention is not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed with an amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a nonelected invention, treat the RCE as proper but do not enter the amendment; give applicant one month/30 days to submit a complete reply. See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03. Use form paragraphs 8.04 or 8.26 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by application type and filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility rule is reiterated in many contexts; examiners must confirm the application's filing type/date before applying 1.114 procedures. If not eligible, a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051) should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition — must file CIP for added matter
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that 'No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated like a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter to the disclosure, the procedure in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available; applicant must file a continuation-in-part application under 37 CFR 1.53(b). See MPEP § 706.03(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: First action final after filing an RCE — conditions and prohibition on new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to filing an RCE may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) are met. It would not be proper to make final a first Office action immediately after the filing of an RCE if the first Office action includes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.09 when it is appropriate to make the first action after filing the RCE final. Observe the extension-of-time policy per 37 CFR 1.136(a) and the cap that statutory reply period will not expire later than six months from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after allowance or Quayle reopens prosecution but issue fee effects apply
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE complying with 1.114 is filed in an allowed application, prosecution will be reopened. If the issue fee has been paid, however, payment of the fee for an RCE and a submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue will not avoid issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RCE is filed before issue fee payment, no 1.313 petition is required. If filed after issue fee payment, a petition under 1.313 must be filed and granted to reopen prosecution; applicant may not obtain a refund of the issue fee. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision withdraws appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Board but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper; the Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE is proper (fee + submission responsive within 1.111), withdraw finality and enter submission; if not fully responsive but bona fide give shortened period (use 7.42.08). If improper (lacking fee/submission), withdraw appeal and treat application per MPEP § 1215.01: if no allowed claim, application abandoned; if at least one allowed claim, pass to issue or give shortened period for formal matters. Use form paragraph 7.42.06 and 7.42.10–7.42.14 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision — notice and entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but before a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of civil action, and the RCE lacks the fee and/or the submission, the examiner should notify the applicant that the RCE is improper using form paragraph 7.42.16. If the time for seeking court review has passed without review being sought, include the form paragraph with the Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment depending on claim status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is filed with the RCE but the fee is missing, indicate whether the submission has been entered. Generally such submission should not be entered, unless the amendment obviously places application in condition for allowance and supervisory approval is obtained. If the application is not eligible under the date rules for 1.114, prepare PTO-2051 to notify applicant continued examination does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for RCE after Board decision — two month window and law of the case
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of an RCE (with fee and submission) after a Board decision, but before filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of civil action, will result in the finality being withdrawn and the submission being considered if timely filed; generally the time period for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencing a civil action is within two months of the Board's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filed within this two-month period and before court review is timely. Note that a Board decision has res judicata effect and is 'law of the case'; arguments alone (without amendment or new showing of facts) will not remove a rejection that was decided by the Board. See MPEP §§ 1216, 706.03(w), and 1214.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible contents of submissions under 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: As set forth in 37 CFR 1.114, a submission may include an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously submitted entered arguments after final that were not persuasive may nevertheless be considered a submission under 1.114 if they are responsive within the meaning of 1.111 to the outstanding Office action. If the submission does not comply with 1.111 use form paragraph 7.42.08; if no compliance use 7.42.04 or 7.42.05 depending on context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to communicate RCE/CPA outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs should be used by examiners to communicate the treatment of CPAs and RCEs and the resulting status: e.g., 7.42.15 (CPA treated as RCE), 7.42.04 (RCE after final rejection), 7.42.05 (RCE after allowance/Quayle), 7.42.06 (RCE after appeal but before Board decision), 7.42.08 (RCE with submission not fully responsive), 7.42.09 (first action final after RCE), 7.42.10–7.42.14 (various appeal-without-submission/fee outcomes), 7.42.16 (after Board decision but before further appeal/civil action without submission/fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Examiner Notes accompanying each form paragraph for bracket insertions (dates, reasons) and applicable eligibility reminders. Use PTO-2051 when appropriate for improper RCE notices in ineligible applications.
